_comment: CR-46 + CR-002: Native binary integrity manifest. Each entry maps a binary file name (as produced by scripts/build/compile_native.sh and discovered by voice_typer.server.native_hotkeys.binary_path._BINARY_NAMES) to its expected SHA-256, build version, and minimum wire-protocol version. CR-002 fix: keys are now the arch-suffixed names that the build actually emits (linux-key-listener-x86_64, linux-key-listener-aarch64, windows-key-listener-x86_64.exe, windows-key-listener-aarch64.exe, macos-key-listener). The pre-CR-002 keys (linux-key-listener, windows-key-listener.exe) are GONE — they did not match the actual built filenames, so get_expected_sha256(path.name) returned None for every arch-suffixed name and verify_native_binary_or_skip silently trusted every binary. At runtime, binary_path.verify_native_binary() hashes the discovered binary with hashlib.sha256 and compares against the sha256 field here. On mismatch (or on a missing/empty manifest entry — CR-002 fail-closed), the factory logs an error and falls back to the legacy backend (pynput / WindowsNativeHotkey / WaylandHotkey). Entries with an empty sha256 (binaries not built in this Linux dev tree) cause verify_native_binary_or_skip to FAIL CLOSED (return False + log ERROR) — production builds MUST populate all five sha256 fields via scripts/build/update_native_manifests.py (run by CI after compile_native.sh). The min_proto_version field is reserved for future wire-protocol version gating (CR-46 follow-up); the loader does not yet enforce it.
